oldContent: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 Kyro AI: Sales Development Representative Anywhere in the World Alabama Sales Management, Sales, Client Relationship Management, Communication Skills, Client Relations, Sales Enablement, and Stakeholder Communication Sales and Marketing Contract <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/6563/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Texas <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://kyro.ai">https://kyro.ai</a> </p> <p>Sales Development Representative (SDR)</p> <p>Location: Remote, non-US based, working US Central Time business hours<br>Experience: 1-3 years in a B2B SDR/BDR role<br>Employment type: Full-time<br>Reports to: Product Manager - Growth</p> <p>ABOUT KYRO AI<br>When a major storm knocks out power, utilities race to mobilize crews and get the lights back on. Kyro AI builds the software behind that effort: workforce and contractor management for electric utilities, storm restoration contractors, and aggregators. We are headquartered in Plano, Texas, and were spun off from Think Power Solutions, so we pair long-standing utility expertise with the pace and ownership of a product company.<br><br><a href="https://kyro.ai/">https://kyro.ai/</a></p> <p>WHY JOIN KYRO<br>- Work that matters: our platform helps communities get power back after storms and keeps a critical, regulated industry compliant.<br>- A growing product suite: StormShield for storm restoration, Kyro Capital for contractor invoice factoring, KORY (our AI copilot), and contractor onboarding and verification.<br>- Credibility from day one: you sell with the backing of real utility relationships and domain know-how.<br>- Close to leadership: direct access to the CEO and product team, and what you hear from customers shapes the roadmap.<br>- Room to grow: a clear path from SDR to Account Executive.<br>- Flexibility: fully remote team.</p> <p>THE ROLE<br>As an SDR, you are the first conversation most utilities and contractors have with Kyro. You will work two segments with very different buying motions:</p> <p>Utilities (enterprise): You will talk to storm response, emergency management, contractor management, supply chain, and procurement leaders. Cycles are long, involve multiple stakeholders, and are often tied to RFIs/RFPs. A win is a qualified discovery meeting or demo handed to the account team.</p> <p>Contractors (SMB to mid-market): You will talk to owners, operations managers, and storm coordinators at line, vegetation, and restoration contractors. Cycles are shorter, phone-first, and owner-led. A win is a demo held and the contractor signed up and onboarded.</p> <p>WHAT YOU'LL DO<br>- Prospect outbound: research target utilities and contractors, build account lists, and reach decision-makers by phone, email, and LinkedIn.<br>- Own the follow-up: run multi-touch cadences, chase no-shows and stalled conversations, and make sure every lead has a dated next step.<br>- Respond to inbound leads the same business day and qualify them before they go cold.<br>- Qualify with rigor: confirm need, timeline, decision process, budget, and compliance requirements before booking.<br>- Book and confirm demos, send reminders, and hand off with clear notes.<br>- Drive conversions: stay with contractors after the demo until they sign up and start onboarding; keep utility opportunities moving to the next stage.<br>- Keep the CRM clean: log every activity, stage change, and next step.<br>- Feed the product team: share objections, competitor mentions, and feature requests from the field.</p> <p>HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED<br>Success is measured on demos held and the conversions that follow. Activity counts are leading indicators, not the goal. KPIs: demos booked, demos held, demo-to-opportunity rate, conversions (contractors signed up and onboarded; utility opportunities advanced to proposal or pilot), pipeline sourced, speed to lead, follow-up coverage (share of open leads with a dated next step), and outreach activity. Targets are set separately for each segment; utility credit weighs meetings and pipeline more than closed conversions.</p> <p>WHAT YOU BRING<br>- 1-3 years as an SDR or BDR in B2B sales, ideally SaaS, with a record of hitting or beating meeting and demo quotas<br>- Disciplined follow-up across phone, email, and LinkedIn without being reminded<br>- Confident cold calling, including with field-oriented buyers who rarely live in their inbox<br>- Clear, concise written communication<br>- Hands-on experience with a CRM and a sales engagement tool (HubSpot, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, or similar)<br>- Comfort with metrics: you track your own funnel and know where deals stall<br>- Ability to learn a technical, regulated domain quickly<br>- Self-directed and organized in a fully remote setting<br>- Native English speaker, available during US Central Time business hours</p> <p>NICE TO HAVE<br>- Experience selling into utilities, energy, construction, field services, or regulated industries<br>- Familiarity with storm restoration, line work, vegetation management, or contractor ecosystems<br>- Exposure to both enterprise (long-cycle) and SMB or self-serve sales motions<br>- Experience selling workforce management, compliance, or fintech products<br>- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience</p> <p>COMPENSATION AND PROBATION<br>- Competitive market base plus uncapped commission. Base is paid bi-weekly and commission quarterly.<br>- Accelerators: 1.5x at 101-125% of quota, 2.0x above 125%.<br>- The first six months are probationary, with performance reviews at 3 and 6 months against ramped KPI targets (demos held, conversions, follow-up coverage). <br>- If targets are not met, Kyro may extend the probationary period or end employment. - - Employment remains at-will during and after probation.</p> <p>WHAT WE OFFER<br>- Competitive base and variable pay<br>- A fully remote role<br>- A clear path to Account Executive for SDRs who consistently hit target<br>- Direct exposure to product and leadership at a company shaping how utilities run storm response</p> <p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative</a></p> Tue, 13 Oct 2026 17:13:53 +0000 Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:13:53 +0000 https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative Airbnb: Senior Manager, Quality, Volume Tiers Anywhere in the World 🇨🇦 Canada California Management and Finance Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/6567/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> United States <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://careers.airbnb.com/life-at-airbnb/">https://careers.airbnb.com/life-at-airbnb/</a> </p> <p>Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost ever

Get certified. Be ready for what comes next.</p> <p>Robotics AI is advancing rapidly, and high-quality video data helps intelligent systems better understand the world around them. The post Z.ai GLM-Legal Beats Claude Fable 5 and Kimi K3 on Harvey LAB appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Z.ai just released GLM-Legal . GLM-Legal is a legal AI model from Z.ai, built on GLM-5.3-Flash and trained for agentic legal work. It targets contract review, evidence analysis and compliance research. The key result is a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) . That is nearly 3x its base model’s 6.7%. For developers, the catch is access: the API is application-only for now. TL;DR Size: Built on GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-total, 18B-active MoE with a 1M-token context and 128K max output. Z.ai lists no separate GLM-Legal parameter count. Runs on: Z.ai’s hosted API only, by application. No public weights. The base model self-hosts on multi-GPU servers via vLLM or SGLang, with FP8 weights. Performance: Top-10 on Harvey LAB at a fraction of frontier cost. Within 2.3 points of the LegalBench leader. Best: 19.17% Harvey LAB task pass rate, #7 of 79 on Vals AI, at $0.15 per test. Worst: 41.83% on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, below its own base model (45.19%). Bottom line: Best: frontier-class legal agent scores at about 1/128 the cost of Claude Fable 5. Worst: gated beta with no price, no weights and slow runs (1h12m per task). What is GLM-Legal? GLM-Legal is a domain-specialized version of GLM-5.3-Flash for law firms, in-house counsel and compliance teams. The base is Z.ai’s first natively multimodal GLM-5 model . It has 320B total parameters with 18B active. It mixes sparse and linear attention to cut long-context serving cost. It reads text, images, video and files, and outputs text. How was GLM-Legal trained? Training ran in 2 stages: Mid-training on expanded legal corpora, to strengthen reasoning from facts to rules to conclusions. Post-training with reinforcement learning across tens of thousands of legal task environments . The Z.ai team also describes the agent harness co-evolving with the model during post-training. Edge cases in training exposed harness bottlenecks. Harness fixes then exposed the model to more realistic constraints. How does GLM-Legal score on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark? Harvey LAB is an open-source benchmark of 1,250 tasks across 24 practice areas . Over 75,000 expert-written rubric criteria grade the work. A task passes only if every criterion passes. Harvey calls this all-pass grading. Vals AI runs the held-out set with 2 LLM judges and internet disabled . Agents get file tools plus docx , pptx and xlsx skills. On that leaderboard, GLM-Legal scores 19.17% and ranks #7 of 79. Its base, GLM-5.3-Flash, scores 6.67%. The 12.5-point lift is the core claim, and an independent evaluator reproduced it. Z.ai’s launch chart shows GLM-Legal ahead of Kimi K3 (12.92%), Claude Fable 5 (11.25%) and GPT-6 Astra (5.42%). Those figures match Vals AI. The chart omits 6 models ranked higher, led by Muse Spark 1.2 at 25.42%. GLM-Legal also passes 92.5% of individual criteria. Top models sit near 90% to 95% on that measure. Does GLM-Legal match frontier models on LegalBench? Roughly. Z.ai claims parity on LegalBench and the Chinese-focused PLawBench without publishing numbers. Vals AI scores GLM-Legal at 86.23% on LegalBench . Claude Fable 5 leads at 88.56% . Kimi K3 scores 86.21% . How does GLM-Legal compare with Kimi K3, Claude Fable 5 and GPT-6 Astra? Vals ran both GLM models at $0.075 / $0.25 per 1M tokens. How can developers access GLM-Legal? Law firms, legal-tech companies and in-house teams can apply for API access . Z.ai has published no price. No GLM-Legal repository exists on Hugging Face as of October 13, 2026. Z.ai says GLM-Legal will come to AutoClaw , its desktop agent app, but gave no date. newContent: MarkTechPost https://www.marktechpost.com/ An Artificial Intelligence News Platform Wed, 14 Oct 2026 05:03:36 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.marktechpost.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/cropped-Favicon-512-x-512-1-1-32x32.png MarkTechPost https://www.marktechpost.com/ 32 32 127842392 Google Releases Gemini 4 Argon API With 1M Token Output Limit https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/13/google-gemini-4-argon-api-release/ Wed, 14 Oct 2026 05:03:34 +0000 https://www.marktechpost.com/?p=82905 Google has made Gemini 4 Argon generally available on the Gemini API, AI Studio and the Gemini app. The sparse MoE model writes up to 1M output tokens and leads the Vals Index at 68.90%. The post Google Releases Gemini 4 Argon API With 1M Token Output Limit appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Google DeepMind has made Gemini 4 Argon generally available to developers, enterprises and paid Gemini subscribers. Gemini 4 Argon is a sparse mixture-of-experts frontier model from Google built for long, multi-step work. Its target domains are coding, finance, legal, science and cybersecurity. Google first announced Argon on September 30 for a small group of cyber defenders. It now reaches the paid Gemini API at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens. The key change for developers is output length: Argon can write up to 1M tokens in one response. TL;DR Size: Parameter count not disclosed (sparse MoE). 1M token window shared by input and output. Runs on: Google’s cloud only, via Gemini API, AI Studio and Gemini platform. Trained on TPUs. No open weights. Performance: Leads Google’s table on knowledge work, long context and video. Mixed on agentic coding. Best: 91.7% on LVBench (long video understanding). Worst: 55.0% on FrontierSWE v2, last of 4 models in Google’s table. What is Gemini 4 Argon? According to the model card , Argon is a new model, not a fine-tune of an earlier Gemini. It is a large-scale sparse MoE transformer with native multimodal support. It accepts text, images, audio and video, and it outputs text. Google trained it on TPUs using JAX and ML Pathways. The knowledge cutoff is March 2026. Google has not disclosed total or active parameter counts. How does the 1M token output limit work? Google raised the output limit to 1M tokens, up from 64K on earlier Gemini models. The model card describes a combined input plus output window of up to 1M tokens. So a long prompt reduces the room left for output. Google documents a new continuation protocol for long decodes in its developer docs and enterprise docs . At introductory pricing, a full 1M token response costs $10 in output tokens. How does Gemini 4 Argon perform on benchmarks? Google compares Argon with GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5. Argon posts the top score on most rows. DeepSWE v1.1: 77.9%, ahead of Opus 5.5 (74.2%) and GPT-6 Astra (74.1%). Vals Index: 68.90%, ranked #1 by Vals AI ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (67.04%). AutomationBench: 51.3%, versus 42.5% for Opus 5.5. Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark: 19.6%, nearly 3x the next model, but still a low absolute score. GraphWalks, 256K to 1M tokens: 84.2%, versus 71.8% for GPT-6 Astra. CWE-bench v1: 68.0%, tied with GPT-6 Astra. Google also reports 87% on the ERQA embodied reasoning benchmark . Read the evaluation methodology before drawing conclusions. Most rival scores are self-reported or pulled from public leaderboards. Argon’s DeepSWE score is self-computed with a mini-swe-agent harness. The rival DeepSWE numbers come from system cards and a leaderboard. Where does Gemini 4 Argon fall short? oldContent: MarkTechPost https://www.marktechpost.com/ An Artificial Intelligence News Platform Wed, 14 Oct 2026 05:03:36 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.marktechpost.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/cropped-Favicon-512-x-512-1-1-32x32.png MarkTechPost https://www.marktechpost.com/ 32 32 127842392 Google Releases Gemini 4 Argon API With 1M Token Output Limit https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/13/google-gemini-4-argon-api-release/ Wed, 14 Oct 2026 05:03:34 +0000 https://www.marktechpost.com/?p=82905 Google has made Gemini 4 Argon generally available on the Gemini API, AI Studio and the Gemini app. The sparse MoE model writes up to 1M output tokens and leads the Vals Index at 68.90%. The post Google Releases Gemini 4 Argon API With 1M Token Output Limit appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Google DeepMind has made Gemini 4 Argon generally available to developers, enterprises and paid Gemini subscribers. Gemini 4 Argon is a sparse mixture-of-experts frontier model from Google built for long, multi-step work. Its target domains are coding, finance, legal, science and cybersecurity. Google first announced Argon on September 30 for a small group of cyber defenders. It now reaches the paid Gemini API at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens. The key change for developers is output length: Argon can write up to 1M tokens in one response. TL;DR Size: Parameter count not disclosed (sparse MoE). 1M token window shared by input and output. Runs on: Google’s cloud only, via Gemini API, AI Studio and Gemini platform. Trained on TPUs. No open weights. Performance: Leads Google’s table on knowledge work, long context and video. Mixed on agentic coding. Best: 91.7% on LVBench (long video understanding). Worst: 55.0% on FrontierSWE v2, last of 4 models in Google’s table. What is Gemini 4 Argon? According to the model card , Argon is a new model, not a fine-tune of an earlier Gemini. It is a large-scale sparse MoE transformer with native multimodal support. It accepts text, images, audio and video, and it outputs text. Google trained it on TPUs using JAX and ML Pathways. The knowledge cutoff is March 2026. Google has not disclosed total or active parameter counts. How does the 1M token output limit work? Google raised the output limit to 1M tokens, up from 64K on earlier Gemini models. The model card describes a combined input plus output window of up to 1M tokens. So a long prompt reduces the room left for output. Google documents a new continuation protocol for long decodes in its developer docs and enterprise docs . At introductory pricing, a full 1M token response costs $10 in output tokens. How does Gemini 4 Argon perform on benchmarks? Google compares Argon with GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5. Argon posts the top score on most rows. DeepSWE v1.1: 77.9%, ahead of Opus 5.5 (74.2%) and GPT-6 Astra (74.1%). Vals Index: 68.90%, ranked #1 by Vals AI ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (67.04%). AutomationBench: 51.3%, versus 42.5% for Opus 5.5. Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark: 19.6%, nearly 3x the next model, but still a low absolute score. GraphWalks, 256K to 1M tokens: 84.2%, versus 71.8% for GPT-6 Astra. CWE-bench v1: 68.0%, tied with GPT-6 Astra. Google also reports 87% on the ERQA embodied reasoning benchmark . Read the evaluation methodology before drawing conclusions. Most rival scores are self-reported or pulled from public leaderboards. Argon’s DeepSWE score is self-computed with a mini-swe-agent harness. The rival DeepSWE numbers come from system cards and a leaderboard. Where does Gemini 4 Argon fall short? Argon trails on 5 rows of Google’s own table: FrontierSWE v2: 55.0%, versus 65.5% for GPT-6 Astra. Terminal-Bench 4.0: 57.4%, versus 66.4% for Opus 5.5. Terminal-Bench Science 0.1: 57.6%, versus 68.1% for GPT-6 Astra. PostTrainBench: 45.3%, versus 49.3% for Opus 5.5. OSWorld-2.0 (offline subset): 69.2%, versus 72.6% for GPT-6 Astra. The model card also lists hallucinations and occasional slowness or timeouts. Under Google’s Frontier Safety Framework, Google says it cannot rule out the biological and cybersecurity critical capability levels. It reports deploying safeguards it assesses as lowering that risk. newContent: MarkTechPost https://www.marktechpost.com/ An Artificial Intelligence News Platform Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:57:31 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.marktechpost.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/cropped-Favicon-512-x-512-1-1-32x32.png MarkTechPost https://www.marktechpost.com/ 32 32 127842392 9 Best AI Gateways in 2026: Bifrost, Portkey, LiteLLM, Kong and 5 More Ranked https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/14/best-ai-gateways-2026/ Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:57:28 +0000 https://www.marktechpost.com/?p=82912 Marktechpost ranks the 9 best AI gateways for 2026. We compare Bifrost, Portkey, LiteLLM, Kong, TrueFoundry, Cloudflare, Vercel, OpenRouter and Orq.ai on latency, pricing, licensing, governance and deployment. The post 9 Best AI Gateways in 2026: Bifrost, Portkey, LiteLLM, Kong and 5 More Ranked appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> An AI gateway is a control layer between your application and model providers. It gives every service one API for many models. It also centralizes routing, retries, failover, caching, budgets and logs. This guide presents the best AI gateways for production teams in 2026. The market moved fast this year. Palo Alto Networks closed its acquisition of Portkey on May 29. Mintlify acquired Helicone , which now runs in maintenance mode. LiteLLM survived a PyPI supply chain compromise in March. Your gateway choice now carries vendor and security risk, not just feature risk. TL;DR Best overall for self-hosted performance: Bifrost. Go binary, Apache 2.0, 11 µs published overhead at 5,000 RPS. Best open-source gateway with guardrails: Portkey. MIT license, 1,600+ models, now backed by Palo Alto Networks. Widest adoption: LiteLLM. 53.8K GitHub stars, 100+ providers, Python-first. Best for API platform teams: Kong AI Gateway. LLM, MCP and A2A traffic in one stack. Best managed options: Cloudflare (edge, free core), Vercel (zero markup), OpenRouter (model access). How We Ranked These AI Gateways We weighted 6 criteria for production use: Performance evidence: published overhead, and how it was measured. Coverage: providers and models behind one OpenAI-compatible API. Governance: virtual keys, budgets, RBAC, audit logs, guardrails. Deployment: self-hosted, VPC, air-gapped, or managed only. Cost model: markup, platform fees, free tier limits. Vendor and supply chain risk: license, ownership changes, security history. Quick Comparison: 9 Best AI Gateways Rank Gateway License Deployment Coverage (vendor claim) Published overhead Entry pricing 1 Bifrost Apache 2.0 Self-hosted, VPC, air-gapped 23+ providers 11 µs at 5K RPS Free OSS; Enterprise custom 2 Portkey MIT (gateway) Self-hosted, managed, private cloud 1,600+ models Under 1 ms Free OSS; hosted from $49/mo 3 LiteLLM Open source + commercial license Self-hosted, hosted 100+ providers 8 ms P95 at 1K RPS Free OSS; Enterprise custom 4 Kong AI Gateway Open core Self-hosted, cloud, hybrid Multi-LLM via plugins Not disclosed Free trial; paid plugins 5 TrueFoundry Proprietary VPC, on-prem, air-gapped, SaaS 1,600+ models Under 3 ms internal Free 30K requests/mo 6 Cloudflare AI Gateway Proprietary Managed edge Major providers + Workers AI Not disclosed Core features free 7 Vercel AI Gateway Proprietary Managed Multi-provider, multimodal Not disclosed Zero token markup 8 OpenRouter Proprietary Managed Major labs + open models Not disclosed 5.5% fee on credits 9 Orq.ai Router Proprietary Managed 400+ models, 20+ providers Not disclosed Free tier 1. Bifrost (Maxim AI) What it is: Bifrost is an open-source AI gateway written in Go. It exposes 23+ providers through one OpenAI-compatible API. It ships under Apache 2.0 and has 8.7K GitHub stars. Why it ranks first: it has the strongest published performance numbers of any self-hosted gateway. The README reports 11 µs added latency at 5,000 RPS on a t3.xlarge. On a t3.medium, that figure is 59 µs. Maxim’s benchmark against LiteLLM reports P99 latency of 1.68 s versus 90.72 s at 500 RPS. Key features: Automatic fallbacks, weighted load balancing and semantic caching. Virtual keys with hierarchical budgets and rate limits in the open-source build. MCP gateway support, plus Code Mode for large tool sets. Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry tracing. Drop-in endpoints for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google GenAI SDKs. Best for: high-throughput teams that must self-host inside a VPC or air-gapped network. 2. Portkey What it is: Portkey’s AI Gateway is an MIT-licensed gateway with 13K GitHub stars. It claims routing to 1,600+ models, under 1 ms latency and a 122 KB footprint. Why it ranks here: it pairs strong routing with the deepest built-in guardrail catalog. A Gateway 2.0 pre-release merges Portkey’s enterprise gateway into open source. Palo Alto Networks now owns Portkey and is folding it into Prisma AIRS. Key features: Fallbacks, retries, conditional routing, load balancing and request timeouts. Simple and semantic caching. Input and output guardrails, with bring-your-own and partner options. MCP Gateway with central auth, access control and tool-call logging. Pricing: Braintrust’s comparison lists a free tier with 10K logged requests. Paid plans start at $49 per month. Best for: teams that want guardrails and routing in one open-source gateway. 3. LiteLLM What it is: LiteLLM is the most widely adopted open-source LLM gateway. It has 53.8K GitHub stars and supports 100+ providers. It ships as a Python SDK and a proxy server. Why it ranks here: coverage and ecosystem depth are unmatched. It supports chat, embeddings, images, audio, batches, rerank, MCP and A2A endpoints. The project reports 8 ms P95 latency at 1K RPS in its own benchmarks . Key features: Virtual keys, per-team spend tracking, budgets and RPM/TPM limits. Router with retries, fallbacks and load balancing across deployments. Admin UI, guardrails and logging to Langfuse, OpenTelemetry and others. Terraform modules for AWS and GCP, plus cosign-signed Docker images. Best for: Python-first teams that need maximum provider coverage and can run the proxy. 4. Kong AI Gateway What it is: Kong AI Gateway extends Kong’s API gateway to AI traffic. It governs LLM, MCP and agent-to-agent (A2A) traffic from one platform. Why it ranks here: Kong brings mature API management to AI. Its site notes Gartner named Kong a leader in API management for the 7th year. Key features: PII sanitization, semantic prompt guards and access control. Semantic caching, routing and load balancing. Best for: enterprises already standardized on Kong for API management. 5. TrueFoundry AI Gateway What it is: TrueFoundry offers an enterprise AI gateway with LLM, MCP and agent gateway features. You should have. Over the past decade, Tosin and his team built Moniepoint into the operating system for more than 6 million Nigerian businesses, processing over $300 billion a year , or 39% of Nigeria’s digital payments volume and 8 out of every 10 in-person payments . As a Nigerian American, I’ve witnessed my father make trips to Western Union to send money back home for decades, and I experienced Nigeria’s fee-laden payment system when visiting the country. Moniepoint is transforming that system. Nnamdi Okike, co-founder and managing partner of 645 Ventures. Moniepoint is not alone. Sea Limited , Grab , Kaspi , Yassir , Nubank 1 — these are companies most Americans have never heard of, despite them being worth several tens or hundreds of billions, following the trail blazed by Tencent , Alibaba and MercadoLibre . These are super apps that bundle banking, commerce, ride-hailing and bill pay into one trusted application. The idea never took hold in the U.S. for one reason: trust is cheap here. With 96% of households already banked , a specialist app inherits the credibility of the financial system. Where trust is cheap, there is no need for a super app. Build trust first In emerging markets, trust is the whole problem. Four conditions tend to precede a super app: High mobile penetration, which makes distribution cheap; weak incumbent competition; poor existing financial services; and the condition most investors screen past, a financial crisis severe enough to strip incumbents of legitimacy. These populations are not merely underbanked. They were harmed, and the institutions that harmed them still hold the market. Brazil froze roughly 80% of bank deposits and financial investments for 18 months in 1990 in an effort to break hyperinflation. The banking consolidation that followed left five banks holding about 80% of banking assets and charging card rates north of 300% . That was the void Nubank was born into. Kazakhstan went through it twice: savings erased by inflation in the thousands of percent when the ruble zone collapsed in 1993, then a 2007–09 banking crisis in which the country’s largest bank, BTA, holding roughly a quarter of the system’s assets, was nationalized and defaulted amid allegations of multibillion-dollar fraud. Kaspi grew into that void. Southeast Asia’s 1997 crisis was harsher still. Indonesia closed 16 banks in a single announcement, the rupiah lost about 85% of its value, and output fell 13 %. Two decades later roughly half of Indonesian adults still had no bank account, which enabled Sea to build Shopee and SeaMoney into that gap. Kaspi also answers the objection I hear most from American investors, which is that these markets are too small to produce large exits. Kazakhstan has only 20 million people, and according to company filings , around 14 million — nearly 70% of its population — use Kaspi. The average user transacts roughly 77 times a month . It earns $9 billion of revenue at 56% EBITDA margins, and its enterprise value is over $17 billion . Depth of spend, not population, sets the ceiling. Compare Nubank to Chime . Nubank has 14x the customers, 127 million to Chime’s 9.5 million , about 7x the revenue and a market capitalization more than 6x larger. Nubank has brought over 31 million previously unbanked Brazilians into the financial system . A technology applied in an overlooked market with a large unaddressed pain point can build a bigger and more defensible company than the same technology applied in a rich one. Screen for the four conditions and a few markets stand out as places where the next super app could emerge: Bangladesh: Five banks looted from the inside for years before the 2024 change in government exposed them , with the government now promising to pay 7.5 million savers whose money is gone. Egypt: Repeated devaluations of the pound between 2016 and 2024, shrinking savings held at banks the state itself owns. Vietnam: Savers pulled 80% of deposits out of one major bank in 2022 after its owner was arrested in a $24 billion fraud. Pakistan: A near-default and 38% inflation in 2023 , then government-built rails and a national ID that makes onboarding nearly costless. One boundary condition: The crisis must be severe enough to delegitimize incumbents but contained enough that the currency and payment rails still work. The first generation of super apps created enormous value for the investors who backed them early. In 2001, the South African media company Naspers paid roughly $34 million for a 46.5% stake in Tencent, a stake later worth more than $100 billion and one of the best tech investments ever made . Sequoia Capital ’s investment in Nubank’s $2 million seed round, combined with its lead Series A investment, was worth $7 billion at the company’s IPO . The second generation is scaling now. The third will be built on stablecoins and AI technologies, in Abidjan, Buenos Aires, Karachi and Lagos, by founders like Tosin Eniolorunda who will play an increasingly important role in the growth of emerging market economies. Nnamdi Okike is co-founder and managing partner of 645 Ventures , where he oversees the firm’s investing strategy, governance and compliance, with a focus on fintech and enterprise technology. Since co-founding 645 Ventures in 2014, he has invested in and partnered with companies including RentSpree , Setpoint , Sequence , Solidus Labs , Order and Uptiq . Previously, he was an investor at Insight Partners , where he invested in 19 companies and had nine exits representing more than $9 billion in exit value. newContent: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Tue, 13 Oct 2026 19:51:14 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.11 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 Exclusive: Stella & Dot Founder Raises $5M For Her Next Act, AI Marketing Startup Marklo https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/founder-raises-5m-next-act-ai-marketing-startup-marklo-herrin/ Wed, 14 Oct 2026 12:00:38 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=94222 Jessica Herrin was pregnant with her first child and working at Dell when she began testing jewelry trunk shows in Austin on nights and weekends. The venture became Stella & Dot , a business that sold more than $2 billion in products through a network of independent sellers. Two decades later, Herrin is building a business around the marketing problems she encountered along the way. She started Marklo in 2025 to help consumer brands decide which products to promote and prepare their campaigns. The startup has now raised $5 million in seed funding, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively. Jessica Herrin, CEO and founder of Marklo AI. (Courtesy photo) Forerunner led the round, joined by Freestyle Capital and angel investors including former Klaviyo and current Shopify leaders. Marklo helps consumer brands plan marketing campaigns using their sales, inventory and past marketing data. Its software shows which promotions drove sales, suggests what products to promote next and uses AI to draft campaign briefs and organize tasks. While Marklo is still pre-revenue, more than 100 brands are already using its software in a pilot, according to Herrin. Those brands include Away , Clare V. , Monica + Andy , Maya Brenner and Latico Leathers . The Burlingame, California-based company is now opening its software to the public ahead of the holiday shopping season. It plans to use its new funding to hire engineers, develop the product and expand customer support. Planning campaigns To decide what to promote next, marketers first need to understand what drove past sales. That can be a challenging endeavor when sales, inventory and marketing records all sit in separate systems. Marklo collects that information from Shopify and services such as Klaviyo, Attentive , Meta and Google , then puts past launches, promotions and sales into a calendar. Teams can see, for example, whether a rise in sales attributed to paid advertising coincided with a new product launch or a widely shared social post — factors they might miss when reviewing each service separately, Herrin said. Marklo can then draft a campaign plan and create related tasks for the team to review, edit and assign. Using those records, along with competitors’ promotions and social media trends, Marklo suggests what a brand should market next. It also considers what the retailer has in stock and when a promotion would run. From there, teams can use the software to plan campaigns, draft marketing materials and assign work, with suggested campaigns and reports also delivered through Slack or email. Herrin said the lack of broader-picture context with other AI tools frustrated her. For example, a tool might identify a Fourth of July sale as a successful promotion and suggest repeating it. “Hey, no, I can’t. It’s not Fourth of July. We don’t have the inventory anymore,” she recalled thinking. In one case, Herrin described how Marklo identified a color trending on social media and a matching handbag a retailer had in stock but hadn’t promoted recently. It offered to plan a post based on one that had performed well before. Latico Leathers offers another example of how a brand uses Marklo. The company used the software to plan a month’s worth of marketing in one day, a process that had previously taken most of a week across meetings, spreadsheets and five tools, according to Herrin. In the end, humans review and approve Marklo’s proposed work. The company says it does not use customer data to train AI models. As for its revenue model, Marklo plans to charge a monthly subscription fee, with additional charges based on usage. For now, brands can install and try it for free. “I’m very passionate about small and medium businesses, and I want to make it accessible to every single brand that runs on Shopify,” Herrin told Crunchbase News in an interview, “so that they can operate like a big brand.” A change of direction The decision to build Marklo followed a change in how Herrin thought about Stella & Dot’s future. That company began as a way for women to earn money on their own schedules by hosting trunk shows in their own homes. It expanded into apparel and skincare and paid out more than $500 million to its sellers, Herrin said. “For me, it was never about the jewelry,” she told Crunchbase News. When COVID-19 put a stop to in-home gatherings, business dropped 80% almost overnight. Herrin also realized that women who might once have signed up to sell Stella & Dot products suddenly had other options. They could promote multiple brands as influencers or open their own Shopify stores. She described Stella & Dot as “the COVID victim that had pre-existing conditions.” Rather than rebuild the old model, Herrin sold the businesses and brands separately. Later, she bought back the Stella & Dot brand to sell through a different channel and test Marklo. She was also reconsidering what she wanted to do next. As she approached her 50th birthday, Herrin questioned whether she would choose to start the same business again. “As an entrepreneur, you don’t just start a business; you start a life,” she said. She still wanted to help people build businesses. What had changed was the problem she wanted to solve: Opening an online store had become easier, but managing its marketing still meant gathering information from several systems and coordinating the next campaign. “The mission was the same, but the solution needed to evolve,” Herrin said. A return to venture capital For Marklo, Herrin also returned to venture funding after relying more on profits to grow Stella & Dot. She had raised venture capital for her first company, which became WeddingChannel.com , but came away feeling that it had raised too much money. She took a different approach with Stella & Dot, building it with about $2 million in capital and a focus on profitability. “Here’s a new growth strategy,” Herrin recalled thinking. “How about profits?” With Marklo, she wanted to hire engineers and develop the software faster. Its 11-person team includes engineers who previously worked at Shopify and Google. She also sought investors with commerce experience. “Raising capital isn’t just about having money for expenses,” Herrin said. “It’s about bringing a brain trust together.” Experience as ‘the customer she’s building for’ Kirsten Green , founder and managing partner of Forerunner Ventures, said Herrin’s experience building Stella & Dot was a central reason for backing Marklo. “Jessica uniquely has been the customer that she’s building for right now at every stage, from starting a brand to having a brand at scale,” Green told Crunchbase News in an interview. That experience gives Herrin firsthand knowledge of where teams lose time, which decisions affect profitability and what brands need before trusting new technology, she added. While AI in general makes it easier to produce marketing content, Green sees the greater opportunity in helping brands decide on what exactly to promote, as well as in understanding the impact on margins and how to grow in ways consistent with their identity. Marklo, she said, incorporates the judgment needed to turn business data into useful recommendations. Get certified. Be ready for what comes next.</p> <p>Robotics AI is advancing rapidly, and high-quality video data helps intelligent systems better understand the world around them. Demonstrate your skills now and be considered when project opportunities become available.</p> </div> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>▌ What you will do</p> <p>As part of the certification process, you will demonstrate your ability to:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Annotate short video clips by identifying objects, actions and events.</p> </li> <li> <p>Evaluate video quality, relevance and accuracy against established guidelines.</p> </li> <li> <p>Assess the clarity and plausibility of movements.</p> </li> <li> <p>Apply instructions consistently and identify potential quality issues.</p> </li> </ul> <p>▌ What you bring</p> <ul> <li> <p>Strong attention to detail and analytical thinking.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong written English and the ability to follow detailed instructions independently.</p> </li> <li> <p>A commitment to accuracy and consistency.</p> </li> <li> <p>No previous AI or robotics experience required.</p> </li> </ul> <p>▌ What the work looks like</p> <p>You may review short videos and be asked to tag objects or actions, rate video clarity or camera angles on a 1 to 10 scale, or assess whether movements are clearly visible and plausible.</p> <p>▌ Why get certified now</p> <p>Completing certification in advance allows you to demonstrate your qualifications and be considered for relevant independent contractor engagements when opportunities become available.</p> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p> <div> <p>Please note:&nbsp; Certification does not guarantee a project engagement, assignment or paid work.
